The published DES/TOPO tuples predict the liquid densities below under
Lithium's benchmark assumptions. S5 and S6 remain separate datasets.
The count table reports attempted (`size`) and numerically admitted (`sum`)
rows. The following AARD table uses admitted rows only and reports percent;
an incomplete table would therefore have an available-subset AARD.
All direct state checks, source uncertainties, exact thermal actions and
local propagated uncertainty scales remain visible in the retained-row table.

```{python}
import json, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path
r = pd.json_normalize(json.loads(Path('results/density-comparison.json').read_text()))
display(r)
display(r.groupby('source.table_label').admitted.agg(['size','sum']))
display(r[r.admitted].groupby('source.table_label').relative_error_percent.agg(lambda v:v.abs().mean()))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(10,4))
for (name,g),ax in zip(r.groupby('source.table_label'),axes):
    ax.scatter(g['source.T_K'].astype(float),g.observed_kg_m3,label='SI measured')
    ax.scatter(g['source.T_K'].astype(float),g.density_kg_m3.where(g.admitted),marker='x',label='Engine')
    ax.set(title=name,xlabel='Temperature (K)',ylabel='Density (kg/m³)')
    ax.legend()
```

The figure compares discrete predictions with observations at their literal
SI temperatures. It introduces no interpolated model curve. Rezaee et al.,
DOI 10.1016/j.fluid.2026.114737, Tables 4 and 6 supply the tuples; SI S5/S6
supply the density rows and standard uncertainties. Their exact retained
paths and source hashes are in `inputs/source/reference-limits.md` and
`results/density-run-identity.json`.

Lithium's benchmark assumptions supply the rounded F/3 DES particle mass,
TOPO mass, DES donor/acceptor self edge, single self-paired TOPO site,
disabled cross association, zero density-stage dispersion interaction and
benchmark pressure. Their values, read-only Lithium paths, hashes and commit
are retained in `inputs/lithium-declarations.json`. The full-formula-unit
mass and later formula-precise average mass are excluded. These choices do
not establish source parity.

Native mass-fraction conversion and density observations use those masses
and the explicit site graph. Each unanchored request selects the liquid
branch through the Engine's density search. The returned branch code is
retained unchanged: the Engine reports `Unspecified` when its finite search
finds a single stable root serving either branch. With multiple stable
roots a liquid request selects the highest stable root. This finite search
does not prove global stability or complete root enumeration.

The numerical limits shown above are relative pressure closure, then the
mass-density identity, inverse mass fractions and composition normalization.
Positive densities and exact pressure slopes and the native convergence
criterion are also required. The exact fixed-pressure thermal density action
uses the returned density as its anchor. Its local uncertainty is
$\sqrt{u_\rho^2+(u_T\,\partial\rho/\partial T|_P)^2}$, assuming independent
temperature and density errors as a Lithium benchmark assumption. It leaves
particle-basis, topology, rounded-parameter and model-form uncertainties
unquantified. An unavailable action does not invalidate a central density.

Density residuals and AARD are descriptive physical comparisons. The paper
fitted Tait-smoothed data; the literal SI rows here need not be its optimizer
inputs. The printed fitted AARDs are source statistics with a different row
basis and are not pass thresholds. This reuse of calibration evidence is
not independent physical validation. The S5/article temperature-range
conflict remains unresolved, and the density discrepancies have no identified
cause. Extraction, aqueous species, complexes and the published A/B reference
conversion remain excluded. Independent delivered review is pending; this
notebook has not been promoted for manuscript use.
